html:
Thurii was a Greek city founded in 444 or 443 BCE on the Gulf of Taranto in southern Italy, near the ruins of Sybaris. Athens under Pericles sponsored it, but it took settlers from all over the Greek world.

Sybaris had been the richest city of Magna Graecia until Croton destroyed it in 510 BCE. Its surviving people tried to refound it and asked Athens for help. The new city soon split between the old Sybarites and the newcomers, and the Sybarites were driven out.

Thurii drew famous names. The historian Herodotus became a citizen and may have finished his book there. The orator Lysias lived there as a young man. Tradition says Protagoras wrote its laws and Hippodamus laid out its streets in a grid.

Athens did not keep control for long. In 282 BCE Thurii asked Rome for help against local Italian peoples, a step that drew Rome into the south and led to the Pyrrhic War.
sum: Thurii was a Greek city founded in 444 or 443 BCE on the Gulf of Taranto in southern Italy, near the ruins of Sybaris. Athens under Pericles sponsored it, but it took settlers from all over the Greek world.
